summary: This is one rule-clean knob: the block_size_m pick goes from 64 to 48 for 512<T<=1024. One run reads cleanly per shape, because turn_4 and first_turn act as built-in controls and SGLang's column also uses 64. Whether it wins depends on how many local experts at T=753 exceed 48 rows, and nobody has measured that, so read the result per shape and against the block-32 sibling.
justification: The mechanism has evidence behind it and the magnitude is consistent. In muse_moe_w4a16 marlin-block-size-m-next-larger (job 2639e3ca7f5549de), bs=128 went 0.8596x when moving 48->64. At ~4 local rows per expert that is about one block per expert, so a tmb3 block costs ~0.85x a tmb4 block. SGLang itself picks 48 at bs=128 on that problem, so the tmb-3 Marlin instantiation for this NVFP4 config already exists and ran. The 'may raise at the first test' risk is effectively moot. At T=753 Marlin (2 launches) is 730.1 us (66.4%) on the sliding shape and 680.7 us (45.4%) on the full shape. It streams ~0.9 GB at ~1.2 TB/s, so it is not byte-bound. Compute is not the limit either: about 2048 padded rows x 50 MFLOP/row x 2 is roughly 0.2 TFLOP, a few hundred us even on mma.sync. So the per-block config cost is the lever. Expected size: 12-15% off Marlin gives ~8-10% on sliding and ~5.5-7% on full. With weights 46/16 the turn_1 load gains ~8%, roughly +2.5% on the 3-load geomean. That is consistent with the stated 6-10% and far above the 1.5-2.5% per-shape drift. turn_4 (T=3012) and first_turn (T=16384) keep 64 and are true controls. Tests T=600 and T=753 change tiling only. Weakest link: the hypothesis asserts 'hot experts reach 30-50 rows' but never measured it. Each local expert above 48 rows adds a second full weight pass at tmb3. At a ~0.85 per-block ratio, break-even is roughly 32*0.15/0.85 = ~5-6 overflow experts out of 32. Routing is correlated across tokens (ROUTER_ALIGN=0.07 along the shared stream-mean direction plus ROUTER_BIAS_STD=0.055 bias), so the tail can be heavier than Poisson around 23.5. The 7% gap in Marlin time between the sliding and full turn_1 shapes (same T) already shows routing load differs per shape. A second, minor weak link: the sister ratio comes from ~4 real rows per block. At ~23 real rows the per-block cost may scale differently if the kernel is partly smem/latency-bound rather than padded-MMA-bound.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity (only landed item): moe_align_block_size runs with N_EXPERTS=256 on remapped ids, where the ~7/8 of routes that are non-local are -1. If SGLang's align buckets -1 routes into skipped (is_ep) blocks, the skipped-block count grows from ~83 to ~110 when moving 64->48. If Marlin's stripe partition counts skipped blocks, part of any delta is load imbalance and not tmb cost. It is not a direction confounder: the muse_moe_w4a16 sister ran the same EP -1 structure, and SGLang's baseline column shares the path. It matters only for attributing the mechanism.
sglang-pipeline-parity: the Triton local-id remap and the use_fp32_reduce/use_atomic_add settings are unchanged by this hypothesis, and LESSONS records those knobs as no-ops. No interaction expected.
interference: No companion is warranted. A gain is unambiguous: one knob changes, only the turn_1 Marlin rows can move, turn_4/first_turn are in-run controls, and the replaced kernel's own time (top_kernels Marlin) shows directly whether the delta is Marlin. A loss is also interpretable: overflow passes outweigh the cheaper blocks at T=753. ab-revert of sglang-pipeline-parity would revert to the starter, which is meaningless. An ab-tune of the cutoff (e.g. 48 only on sliding) branches on layer type, not on T, and would not isolate anything. Splitting 'cheaper tmb3 block' from 'more blocks' is impossible through the public API. The sibling experts-marlin-block-m-local-rows (block 32, same base, same shapes) already serves as the second point on the cost curve, so the pair brackets 64/48/32 without extra runs. Dispatch both on the same master base and compare per-shape Marlin µs directly. The loser is the A/B. Do not stack one on the other.
open_questions: How many of the 32 local experts exceed 48 (and 32) rows at T=753 on the scored inputs? If the implementer can compute a routing histogram offline (outside the timed call, e.g. a local script on reference inputs), it would explain a flat or split result. Do not add any device->host read inside kernel_fn.

Sliding and full turn_1 may split, since their Marlin times differ by 7% at the same T, which suggests different routing skew. A per-layer-type pick (branching on config['window']) is legal, but adopt one only after the split repeats, not on one run.
Confirm from the profile that the Marlin kernel launched with the tmb-3 template (kernel name or grid) at turn_1, and that turn_4/first_turn kernel times are within ~1% of 62025c368c3c4e8e.
If both 48-turn1 and 48-turn4 win, combine them as one T->block table in a stacked follow-up. They touch disjoint T ranges, but each was measured against master alone.

Check moe_align_block_size's sorted_ids/expert_ids buffer sizing at block 48 with num_experts=256 (non-power-of-two block). It is SGLang's own code path at bs=128 on the sister problem, so expect it to be fine.
